name: Liquid Death
why: Death-metal branding for... water. Skulls, 'Murder Your Thirst', horror-comedy product videos and merch drops - the site feels like a band page, not a beverage store.
steal: Total commitment to a bit. Pick one exaggerated brand universe and never break character anywhere on the site.

name: Recess
why: Dreamy surrealist world - floating objects, pastel gradients, hypnotic scroll physics, a can-shaped cart that fizzes on hover. Site is designed to make you feel the calm the drink sells.
steal: Make the site itself deliver the product's emotional promise. Micro-interactions (cart, hover, scroll) as brand moments.

name: Vacation
why: An entire fictional 1980s resort corporation - fake employee ID cards, Miami-vice type gradients, 'leisure-enhancing' copy, even a business-card generator that made users 'employees'.
steal: World-building over web design. Give visitors a role inside the brand story, not just a catalogue.

name: Poolsuite
why: The whole site is a working retro Macintosh desktop - draggable windows, summer radio channels, pixel UI. One of the most screenshotted websites on the internet.
steal: An interface metaphor (old OS, magazine, boutique) can make a site unforgettable on its own.

name: MSCHF
why: Chaotic anti-brand that ships a bizarre product every two weeks - the site is a numbered archive of stunts. No hero banners, no funnel, pure intrigue.
steal: Scarcity + numbered drops + zero explanation creates cult curiosity. Works for limited capsule collections.

name: Starface
why: Y2K smiley-star universe on a .world domain - acid yellows, chunky cursors, mascot-led everything. Made acne care loud instead of clinical.
steal: Flip the category's visual code. If everyone whispers elegance, shout play (or vice versa). Also: unusual TLDs (.world, .inc) set tone before the site loads.

name: Omsom
why: 'Proud + loud' - neon colour blocking, giant type, unapologetic founder-story energy. The brand voice is the design.
steal: A strong point of view (cultural pride, boldness) expressed typographically beats generic 'premium minimal'.

name: Graza
why: Made olive oil fun - squeeze-bottle mascot illustrations, hand-drawn scribbles, chef-meme energy. Turned a commodity into a personality.
steal: Illustration systems give infinite, ownable brand assets - cheaper and more distinctive than photoshoots.

name: Fishwife
why: Maximalist illustrated tins turned into a whole site aesthetic - riso-print colours, wallpaper patterns, editorial recipes. Tinned fish as a lifestyle.
steal: Let packaging art direct the website - one continuous visual system from product in hand to pixels.

name: Aura Bora
why: Storybook surrealism - talking animal characters, 'Aura Bora Land' page, whimsical illustrated flavour worlds for basil-and-lavender water.
steal: Flavours/collections as illustrated 'worlds' - could map beautifully to fabric/craft stories.

name: Surreal
why: Meme-first copywriting famous for celebrity-endorsement spoofs ('endorsed by a guy named Ronaldo'). The website reads like a stand-up set.
steal: Copywriting IS design. A witty voice makes even a simple Shopify layout feel crazy.

name: Magic Spoon
why: Saturday-morning-cartoon nostalgia rebuilt for adults - hyper-saturated 3D cereal worlds, floating loops, retro-future type.
steal: Nostalgia, executed at premium quality, converts. Pick an era your audience loves and modernise it.

name: Dr. Squatch
why: Lumberjack-bro comedy empire - viral infomercial videos embedded everywhere, 'manly' copy pushed to parody levels.
steal: Video-led landing pages with a repeatable comedic format build recall fast.

name: Tushy
why: Sells toilet hygiene with relentless poop puns, peach emojis and taboo-breaking cheek. Made an awkward category shareable.
steal: Humour dissolves category awkwardness - useful anywhere purchase anxiety exists (fit, body, price).

name: Who Gives A Crap
why: Charity-meets-comedy - bold striped wrap design, cheeky name, 50% of profits to sanitation, on a .org that sells product.
steal: Mission + mischief together. Do-good messaging doesn't have to be earnest and beige.

name: Chubbies
why: 'Weekend apparel' worldview - every product name, photo and microcopy is a joke about Friday-at-5pm freedom.
steal: Sell an occasion/feeling (the weekend) rather than a garment. Chiku could own 'the 9-to-9 power drape' the same way.

name: Not Pot
why: Web-1.0 cuteness - pixel bears, pastel chaos, hand-made vibes with an anti-corporate wink. Feels like a friend's weird homepage.
steal: Deliberate lo-fi/DIY aesthetics read as honest and young against polished competitors.

name: Ghia
why: Matisse-esque Mediterranean art direction - sculptural product photography, sun-baked palette, feels like a Riviera gallery not a store.
steal: Art-book restraint is its own kind of crazy. Premium can mean gallery, not luxury-template.

name: Palace Skateboards
why: Legendary absurdist product descriptions - each item gets a nonsense poem instead of specs. People visit just to read them.
steal: One tiny recurring surface (product descriptions) done weirdly can become the thing people share.

name: Glossier
why: The D2C benchmark - built from a blog community outward; millennial-pink minimalism, UGC-as-content, 'skin first' editorial commerce.
steal: Community and content before catalogue - the site feels like a magazine you can shop.

name: Snif
why: Gen-Z fragrance without the French-perfume pretence - loud colour, blunt names, try-before-you-buy model front and centre.
steal: De-snob a premium category: plain talk + bold visuals + risk-free trial.

name: Feastables
why: Creator-economy commerce - gamified packaging, sweepstakes baked into the product, chunky game-UI design language.
steal: Gamification (codes, prizes, drops) turns buyers into repeat players - and creators into distribution.

name: Ffern
why: You can't just buy it - you join 'the ledger'. Four seasonal fragrances a year, made to order in Somerset only for ledger members, released on the solstice/equinox. The site reads like a nature almanac.
steal: Membership-by-ledger + seasonal releases = built-in scarcity and ritual. A 'made only for those on the list' model would feel deeply premium for limited weave collections.

name: Flamingo Estate
why: The brand IS a real 7-acre LA hillside estate - products come 'from the garden', shot in lush editorial style; started as pandemic produce boxes for friends.
steal: Anchor the brand to a real physical place with a story. 'From our ateliers in ___' gives provenance a home and every product a setting.

name: Bode
why: One-of-a-kind garments cut from antique quilts, grain sacks and Victorian linens - every product page is a tiny history lesson; luxury built on textile memory.
steal: The most relevant reference for chiku: one-of-one pieces from heritage textiles, with the fabric's story told on the product page itself.

name: Story mfg.
why: 'Grown, not made' - plant-dyed, hand-loomed psychedelic clothing with a Positive Product Manifesto; craft ideology presented like an art zine.
steal: Publish a manifesto page. Stating what you refuse to do (synthetic dyes, fast drops) is a luxury signal in itself.

name: Officine Universelle Buly 1803
why: A 19th-century Parisian apothecary resurrected in 2014 (now LVMH) - engraved typography, calligraphy services, water-based perfumes; the site feels like stepping into 1803.
steal: Commit to a period aesthetic completely - type, language, packaging, even services (their calligraphy = your monogramming/embroidery personalisation).

name: Brunello Cucinelli
why: Sells cashmere through philosophy - 'Humanistic Capitalism', the restored village of Solomeo, letters from the founder quoting Greek philosophers. The site is half store, half moral essay.
steal: A founder worldview, written in the founder's voice, elevates product into belief. Luxury customers buy the philosophy first.

name: Gentle Monster
why: Korean eyewear label famous for surreal kinetic-robot store installations - the site carries the same sci-fi art-exhibition energy; products presented like museum objects.
steal: Treat campaigns as art installations, not photoshoots. One jaw-dropping set piece per collection gives the site (and press) something to talk about.

name: Aesop
why: Literary luxury - literary quotes woven throughout, muted interiors, every store architecturally unique and documented on the site like a design journal.
steal: Restraint + intelligence as brand voice. Quoting poetry/literature (Indian poets, in chiku's case) makes a commerce site feel cultured, not salesy.

name: Freitag
why: Every bag is cut from a used truck tarpaulin, so no two are alike - the site sells individual bags photographed one by one, plus a SWAP platform for circular exchange.
steal: When products are one-of-a-kind, photograph and sell each piece individually - uniqueness becomes the shopping experience.

name: Sézane
why: French-girl commerce as a journal - numbered weekly drops, archive raffles via 'La Liste', philanthropy programme woven in; feels like a Paris apartment, not a store.
steal: Journal-style merchandising + small numbered drops + a waitlist for archive pieces - premium womenswear mechanics proven at scale.
